summary: The instruction and delegated docs form a coherent large-system contract, and most authority, rollout, stream, readiness, eligibility, and recovery behaviors are bidirectionally aligned. However, several material instruction requirements (least-connections selection, draining, passive ejection, audit exposure) have no meaningful verifier coverage, while at least two F2P tests enforce persistence/API details not discoverable from the solver-visible contract. Q4 cannot certify fair bidirectional alignment until those gaps and phantom couplings are closed.

evidence.observation: Twenty concise bullets state build scope, canonical validation, revision/idempotency fencing, control protocol, quorum rollout, TCP proxy semantics, balancing policies, eligibility composition, draining, PROXY v2, checkpoint recovery, bounded observability, lab inventory, exclusions, and idempotency across operations.
Defines desired-document schema, balancing policies round_robin/least_connections/source_hash, zone and fail-open semantics, health and passive policy fields, canonical ordering, and limits.

Specifies eligibility composition including draining and passive ejection, selector algorithms, bounded buffering/backpressure, half-close, connect/idle timeout behavior, single PROXY v2 header rule, and drain lifecycle.

Documents generation directory contents (snapshot.json, digest, complete), CURRENT advisory semantics, idempotency record binding, and checkpoint verification without naming authority.json or fixed-width directory padding.

Requires bounded readiness/status/metrics/audit views, forbids payload logging, and states generation must not appear as a metric label; does not define rollout_present or other management JSON field names.
Documents build via /app/sovereign-lb/bin/build, operator entrypoints under /app/sovereign-lb/bin/, POST /v1/apply with Idempotency-Key, and inspection of audit/readiness/metrics surfaces.

Thirty-two behavioral pytest cases cover authority conflicts, canonical validation, rollout quorum and preservation, TCP echo/PROXY/half-close/RR/hash, readiness gating, bounded metrics labels, zone/fail-open/incarnation eligibility, and checkpoint restart/fallback; several instruction bullets have no corresponding assertion.
Maps tests to REQ_* families and F2P/P2P classification only; used for boundary labeling, not as spec authority.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction bullet 12 and configuration.md require least_connections balancing, but the verifier only exercises round_robin and source_hash. A solution omitting least_connections selection can pass while violating a stated balancing contract.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a behavioral scenario with concurrent or sequential connections that proves least_connections prefers the lower active-connection target, or narrow the instruction/docs if the policy is intentionally out of scope.
findings.regression_risk: Adding a concurrency-sensitive selector test may flake if connection accounting is racy; use deterministic lab backends and bounded waits.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction bullets 13-14 and dataplane.md require draining: stop new assignment while owned connections continue until deadline. No test deregisters or drains a target and checks both blocked new selection and continued ownership.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a rollout that marks a target draining/deregistered, open a pre-existing connection, assert new connects avoid the target while the owned stream completes or times out at drain deadline.
findings.regression_risk: Drain timing tests can become flaky; anchor on deterministic lab behavior and documented drain_timeout_ms rather than wall-clock sleeps alone.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction bullet 13 and dataplane.md require passive ejection to affect eligibility, and scenario fixtures define passive thresholds, yet no test drives connect/stream failures to eject a target and verify it is skipped until recovery.
findings.minimal_remediation: Use the reset or repeated failure lab backend to trigger passive ejection and assert subsequent selection excludes the ejected incarnation until the configured window elapses or active recovery clears it.
findings.regression_risk: Passive health windows can be timing-sensitive; prefer lab backends with deterministic failure modes and read health counts from bounded status views.

findings.why_it_matters: test_f2p_accepted_digest_persisted requires control_state/authority.json with accepted_digest, but recovery.md never names authority.json or that field, and the shipped revision store schema persists accepted_revision/records only. Equivalent implementations persisting digest solely under documented generation directories would fail grading.
findings.minimal_remediation: Replace the authority.json field assertion with a contract-visible check such as generation directory digest/content alignment already used elsewhere, or document accepted digest persistence in recovery/observability if it is truly required.
findings.regression_risk: Loosening to generation-directory-only checks preserves the material digest invariant while reducing layout coupling.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction bullet 17 and operations.md require bounded audit views, and the control plane exposes GET /v1/audit, but no test verifies audit emission, bounded event shape, or absence of payload/source identity fields after apply.
findings.minimal_remediation: After a successful apply, fetch /v1/audit and assert at least one bounded event with documented fields and no forbidden payload or address material.
findings.regression_risk: Low if assertions stay schema-level and do not require exact timestamps or ordering beyond bounded ring semantics.

findings.why_it_matters: test_f2p_status_reports_rollout_present requires JSON field rollout_present on GET /v1/status, but observability.md only describes rollout phase/quorum summaries and never defines that boolean field name. A compliant status payload exposing rollout object without rollout_present would fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Document rollout_present (or an equivalent explicitly named presence indicator) in observability/operations, or assert on documented rollout.phase/quorum fields instead of a private boolean.
findings.regression_risk: Renaming the assertion to documented rollout.phase preserves behavioral intent with less API coupling.

findings.why_it_matters: test_f2p_checkpoint_generation_directory_padding requires a 20-digit zero-padded generation-00000000000000000001 directory under dataplane state, but recovery.md only says generation directories without fixed-width naming. Semantically equivalent checkpoint layouts would fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Document the generation directory naming convention in recovery.md if it is normative, or assert recovery via status/active_generation and verified snapshot contents rather than exact padding width.
findings.regression_risk: Documenting the existing %020d layout matches current repository behavior and avoids silent oracle-only knowledge.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction bullet 10 and dataplane.md require connect timeout and idle timeout behavior, but tests never force a slow/unreachable backend or idle stall to prove teardown. Current stream tests partially cover buffering and half-close only.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add deterministic timeout scenarios using lab slow/unreachable backends and short configured thresholds, asserting bounded teardown without hanging connections.
findings.regression_risk: Timeout tests need careful deadline budgeting to remain deterministic under verifier load.

findings.why_it_matters: Observability.md states generation must not be a metric label, yet test_f2p_metrics_labels_bounded allows up to two generation= lines after five applies. A non-conformant implementation could retain generation labels and still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Tighten the assertion to forbid generation= labels entirely, or document bounded retention if that is intended and test the documented ceiling.
findings.regression_risk: Stricter label checks may fail starter metrics code until repaired; that is appropriate if the doc rule is normative.

findings.why_it_matters: The instruction uses all twenty allowed bullets and reads as a dense functional checklist spanning nearly every verifier family. It remains a legitimate engineering work request, but reverse-outline similarity to test topology is elevated for a cold solver.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optionally regroup bullets by operational responsibility without deleting requirements; keep material goals in instruction.md rather than relocating them into docs.
findings.regression_risk: Pure regrouping is low risk if no requirements are omitted.

do_not_change: Core REQ_AUTHORITY, REQ_CANONICAL, REQ_ROLLOUT, REQ_STREAM, REQ_READINESS, REQ_ELIGIBILITY, and REQ_RECOVERY scenarios that already align
Delegated technical docs that remain legitimate architecture/protocol references
F2P/P2P boundary intent in the test map
Negative scope exclusions (no HTTP routing, DNS, cloud provisioning)
next_gate: Route req-gaps to Q2 Verifier Coverage Repairer and phantom/interface couplings to Q1/Q3 as needed; rerun cold Q4 after instruction, docs, and verifier updates at the same task_commit.
